liveCommentary.text:
The crucial times and dates you need to know. The Australian Grand Prix weekend begins on Friday March 06. The cars will take to the track for FP1 at 12:30 local time, which is 01:30 UTC.  
  
  
Australia is a standard race weekend, so there are three practice sessions before Qualifying, and then the race on Sunday, March 08.  
  
  
Lights out for that is 15:00 local time, 04:00 UTC.  
  
  
We will be back for live coverage of every bit of track action, but in the meantime, keep your eyes on F1.com for all the latest news as the 2026 season gets ever closer to being fully underway.
liveCommentary.title: Australia next up

liveCommentary.text:
Six days of testing has come and gone. We have quick cars, new processes and what could be a very different pecking order. But of course, we will not know for sure until we get to Qualifying in Australia.   
  
  
There is so much to be excited for, not least the fact that there is always a chance Melbourne will deliver a wet opening race. No one has properly driven these cars in the wet yet - a few filming days were in less favourable conditions, but on those the drivers were barely pushing, and since then all the cars have been heavily upgraded.  
  
  
So all in all, that first race cannot come quickly enough.
liveCommentary.title: Who is excited for the first race?

liveCommentary.text:
Leclerc managed 132 laps, impressive but not the best. Lindblad managed 167 laps, and Sainz 143 today.  
  
  
Contrast that to Stroll, who lapped just six times.  
  
  
There is plenty of work to do for everyone, but Aston Martin really need to get their heads down and come up with some fixes prior to Melbourne.
liveCommentary.title: The lap counts

liveCommentary.text:
As the third day draws to a close, Leclerc is left with the fastest time not just of the day, but across both tests.  
  
  
He set a 1m 31.992s to wind up nearly nine tenths of a second quicker than Norris, with Verstappen over a second back in third.
liveCommentary.title: Leclerc fastest as pre-season testing ends

liveCommentary.text:
One last practice start before the real thing. Russell is on pole, and he gets away quite well. So does Leclerc, who has a little dart down the outside before settling into P2. Leclerc did start from the P5 grid box though.  
  
  
The Audi looked slow off the line, and the Red Bull was a touch slow as well. Food for thought? Melbourne cannot come quickly enough.
liveCommentary.title: Russell on pole for the start

liveCommentary.text:
The red flag period has ended, so 10 cars have opted to come back out for a practice start. But first, we get an extra Formation Lap.  
  
  
So, who is missing? Aston Martin, who called time on their day quite awhile ago.
liveCommentary.title: Time for a practice start

liveCommentary.text:
Here are those checks then, the red flags flying one last time.   
  
  
The cars all come back to the pit lane, but some will go back out as soon as they are allowed to take part in a practice start.
liveCommentary.title: The red flags come out

liveCommentary.text:
Into the final 10 minutes, so these tests could come at any time. As such, Norris is pushing as much as he can to gain some more data.  
  
  
Just a reminder if you are just joining us, Norris missed nearly two hours of running in this session after McLaren completed some precautionary changes over the lunch break, so he is playing catch up a little bit.
liveCommentary.title: Norris keeps lapping

liveCommentary.text:
Here comes Bortoleto on a push lap. But he gets a bit of traffic in the form of Bottas. He is seventh, 1.7s off the pace.  
  
  
But he has completed 70 laps, to go with the 64 that Hulkenberg managed this morning, so Audi's reliability looks to be in a fairly good place.
liveCommentary.title: Bortoleto out on the C4 tyre

liveCommentary.text:
With the clock ticking down and conditions perfect for racing, it is no surprise that the track is quite a busy place at the moment. Russell is chasing down Norris, Bearman has a chunk of track to himself, and Verstappen can see Lindblad ahead.   
  
  
Busy times as the end of testing draws nearer, with the last 10 minutes or so always given over to systems checks to make sure everything is working as it should at Race Control.
liveCommentary.title: Seven cars out on track

liveCommentary.text:
Another hot lap by Leclerc, another quick time. He sets a 1m 31.992s on the C4 tyre, now nearly nine tenths clear of Norris in P2 who to be fair, is not chasing lap time at the moment.   
  
  
Ferrari must be confident in their long run pace if they are already happy to give so much time to hot laps today - which bodes very well for the Scuderia heading into the season.
liveCommentary.title: Leclerc goes even quicker

liveCommentary.text:
If you were not with us earlier, Aston Martin called time on their day with Stroll completing just six laps. They have been struggling with both power unit components and also reliability.  
  
  
When you compare that to Racing Bulls, who have Lindblad out there on his 156th lap, and you can see the size of the deficit facing Aston martin heading to Australia.
liveCommentary.title: Aston Martin lacking laps

liveCommentary.text:
Norris is on the C3 rubber, and he is on a race simulation run of sorts - eight laps and counting as he continues to try and make up for that earlier lost time.   
  
  
Leclerc has just come back out too, so whatever the crew were fixing has clearly been completed.
liveCommentary.title: Norris starts a longer run

liveCommentary.text:
Ferrari are working on their car, so a wall of mechanics have appeared to block as much as they can from prying cameras.   
  
  
Verstappen is still out on track for Red Bull right now, and he is on fresh medium tyres for this run. He is also weaving heavily - that seems to be something we will see a lot of this year.
liveCommentary.title: The wall of mechanics reappears

liveCommentary.text:
Leclerc remains on top at the moment, with a 1m 32.655s. But Norris is now just two tenths back, while Verstappen in third is over six tenths back.  
  
  
The top two are well down in the 1m 32's though, a second faster than the quick times from the first test.  
  
  
And a lot of cars really do seem to be pushing out there.
liveCommentary.title: The times keep dropping

liveCommentary.text:
"Always a pleasure to watch F1 cars trackside at this time of the day in Bahrain, even more so when it's the final session of pre-season testing and drivers are getting stuck into some qualifying simulations," says F1.com's Mike Seymour.  
  
  
"It's striking just how much more the they are pushing their new challengers compared to the start of pre-season testing, and the Barcelona Shakedown before that. A lot of sparks being thrown up as the cars flick through Turn 9 and hit the brakes for Turn 10."
liveCommentary.title: View from the side of the track

liveCommentary.text:
The sun might be gone, but the sky is still lit up with shades of orange and pink. It looks absolutely stunning out there, and these are the conditions the teams will have when they race here in April.   
  
  
The race itself will begin around 10 minutes before sunset, and then finish under the lights in the night time conditions.   
  
  
As such, any running in this last hour or so is by far the most representative.
liveCommentary.title: The sky lights up

liveCommentary.text:
Norris drops into P2 but here comes Leclerc and he.... Goes even faster. The Ferrari man is now a mighty seven tenths ahead of the World Champion.  
  
  
Cause for optimism for the tifosi? Quite possibly...
liveCommentary.title: Norris improves to P2

liveCommentary.text:
Lindblad has been in the car all day for Racing Bulls, and he is up to 140 laps. The most we have seen in a day is Piastri's 161 from last week for reference.  
  
  
But for a rookie driver, who has been working on his fitness all winter to make sure he is sharp for the new season, this is a very strong effort today.
liveCommentary.title: A huge stint for Lindblad

liveCommentary.text:
Norris goes fourth - but it looks like he has more to give, and he had some understeer on that lap too.   
  
  
Just a reminder about the times in testing, as much as we would love to read plenty into the leaderboard, fuel loads are an unknown and so are engine modes.   
  
  
We have some data we can use to hazard a guess over who looks good, but the full pecking order will be revealed in Australia.  
  
  
Reliability though, that we can see from testing.
liveCommentary.title: Norris up to fourth

liveCommentary.text: As the sun begins to set, Norris is weaving down the main straight, building temperature in his tyres - so it looks like he is potentially going for a push lap here. As a result, we will keep an eye on the times...
liveCommentary.title: Norris continues to run

liveCommentary.text:
That is a sizeable wobble for the Ferrari man, who is on a push run. He has lowered his time again too, down to a 1m 33.162s, but on his next lap runs very, very wide as the back tries to step out.   
  
  
He is not the only one either, Russell has jumped up to third and Bortoleto is pushing now too.
liveCommentary.title: Leclerc has a moment

liveCommentary.text:
Finally, Norris is able to get his session underway. He is out around 25 minutes before sunset, so does at least have the best of the track conditions to enjoy.  
  
  
He is out on the C3 medium rubber.
liveCommentary.title: Norris comes out

liveCommentary.text:
Okay, let's update you on how the afternoon session is going as we approach the two-hour mark.   
  
  
Leclerc remains top from Antonelli and Verstappen, the Ferrari man having marginally lowered his time from the morning session.  
  
  
Norris has not made it out yet after McLaren opted to do some work on his car between sessions, while Aston Martin have called time on their day at an early stage.   
  
  
A fair few cars have skated wide as they continue to push the limits, and we have seen some drivers getting some cheeky overtaking practice in too.   
  
  
And the track temperature has dropped down to 31 Degrees as the afternoon heads towards sunset.
liveCommentary.title: Nearly halfway through

liveCommentary.text:
"We have completed our programme for today."  
  
  
That is the message Aston Martin have released, with our reporters saying that Stroll has just left the garage.   
  
  
He completed just six laps today, none of them timed.  
  
  
This is far from ideal for the team here - 128 laps for them in the second test.
liveCommentary.title: Aston Martin have 'completed' their programme

liveCommentary.text:
Approaching the halfway mark in this session, and still Norris has not been out. But the garage is open, and the car is starting to be rebuilt down there.   
  
  
Reportedly, they spotted an issue in the data late in the morning session, and started the work to identify and fix it over the lunchbreak - the words being used in the paddock are 'precautionary change'.   
  
  
But in the meantime, Norris is missing some running...
liveCommentary.title: Norris is still not out

liveCommentary.text:
Verstappen was properly pushing there, and looked set to lower his best time until he ran wide. Grip here is always at a premium for various reasons, and the drivers are definitely testing the limits in these new cars.   
  
  
Better run wide now, than during the race here in August...
liveCommentary.title: Verstappen runs wide

liveCommentary.text:
Leclerc has gone fractions quicker than he did earlier on, the benchmark now a 1m 33.629s.   
  
  
He has completed 91 laps now, having been in the car all day. And there are plenty of reasons for Ferrari to be optimistic this season by the looks of things - their starts look good, they are competitive in terms of times and their tech team might have got a jump on the rest with their rear wing.
liveCommentary.title: Leclerc lowers his benchmark

liveCommentary.text:
Russell was just debating a little bit of overtaking practice, as he closed in on Gasly in the Alpine.   
  
  
How the drivers approach overtaking this year will be fascinating. They have Boost, they have Overtake Mode - but while the cars have less drag down the straights, they also have slightly less downforce into the corners.   
  
  
As such, braking late might be the way forward, but could easily lead to lock ups.   
  
  
One things is for sure, the drivers need to learn the best way forward, and whoever adapts quickest could well deliver some big results and shake up the pecking order.
liveCommentary.title: Back to the action

liveCommentary.text:
Whilst on the subject of Active Aero and rear wings, Ferrari raised the most eyebrows of anyone this test with their interpretation, which flips all the way round. It is interesting, it is innovative and it is legal.   
  
  
But is it quick? That remains to be seen.
liveCommentary.title: Ferrari and the upside down rear wing

liveCommentary.text:
There is also some new terminology to get used to this year.   
  
  
'Boost' is the button the drivers press to use that battery power, and they can do so in attack or defence.   
  
  
'Overtake Mode' is a replacement for DRS - this gives the driver an extra burst of energy. If they are within a second of the car in front, they can use this on the following lap.   
  
  
'Recharge' is how the drivers get their battery back up to full power - and they can do this through braking, lifting and costing, or changing down through the gears.   
  
  
And then there is 'Active Aero'. This is where the front and rear wings flatten out to reduce drag down the straight. Those revert back to their usual shape for the corners. In the wet, the front wing will still move but the rear wing will not open.
liveCommentary.title: New terminology

liveCommentary.text:
An hour into the afternoon session, and let's take a look at the new rules and regulations for 2026.  
  
  
First up, new engines - these are now close to 50/50 between fuel and battery in terms of where the power comes from.   
  
  
The fuel itself is new, and has been trialled in F2 and F3.   
  
  
The chassis is new, and is smaller than last year to create a more 'nimble' car. The tyres are narrower too, so that is another new component for the teams to get to grips with...
liveCommentary.title: The new rules and regulations

liveCommentary.text:
Leclerc remains on top of the timing sheets for the time being - we expect the lowest fuel runs to come later on, in the final hour once the sun has set.   
  
  
The Monegasque driver has completed 84 laps now, but he likely won't be the first to hit a century today, as Lindblad is already on 97 and counting.  
  
  
But one thing that the experts have noticed is that Ferrari seem to be better on their tyres than some in these hot conditions... Another positive for them.
liveCommentary.title: Leclerc continues his run plan

liveCommentary.text:
Norris has not been out this afternoon yet, and nor has Bortoleto. McLaren did have a small issue this morning, that kept Piastri off the track for about half an hour midway through the session.  
  
  
Audi though had a very solid morning, with Hulkenberg managing 64 laps in his final session in the car.
liveCommentary.title: A couple of cars yet to go out

liveCommentary.text:
Speaking of Mercedes, Russell is out. The team changed their PU after an issue for Antonelli this morning. They also had a change a PU last week too... But despite those two issues, the team have completed a monstrous amount of laps across both tests and the Shakedown.   
  
  
Russell has by far the lion's share of the luck, most of the technical or reliability issues have affected Antonelli's running not his.
liveCommentary.title: Russell comes out for Mercedes

liveCommentary.text:
We have been hearing from some of the drivers over the lunch break, and they had quite a few interesting things to say.  
  
  
"Top teams look good as well – Ferrari looked strong this morning and also McLaren and Red Bull. Think top four are close together and will be a tight fight," said Antonelli.  
  
  
Is he right? Could we be in for a four-team fight for the title?   
  
  
It is making Melbourne an even more tantalising prospect - two weeks to go folks, two weeks to go.
liveCommentary.title: A tight fight at the top

liveCommentary.text:
Hands up, who is excited to see Lindblad in action this season?! The teenager has shown plenty of promise not just in his junior career, but in F2 as well. He also impressed when running in FP1 sessions as a 'Friday driver' last season - hence his promotion to a fulltime F1 seat.  
  
  
He is the only rookie on the grid though, and that in itself carries some pressure as he cannot rely on any fellow rookies to compare himself against.
liveCommentary.title: Lindblad heads out

liveCommentary.text:
Bearman is out for Haas, having sat out the morning session. He is joined on the track by Stroll.  
  
  
Haas had a great morning - Ocon managed the most laps of anyone with 82, looked quick and even had time to test out the intermediate tyre.  
  
  
But a quick word on Aston Martin, Stroll was in the garage for most of the morning session and due to battery issues, will only be completing short runs this afternoon. You can read more on that here.
liveCommentary.title: The cars start to come out

liveCommentary.text: The lights go green, but there is no immediate action. A few teams need to finish up those seat changes, while others might be analysing the run plan one last time.
liveCommentary.title: The final session begins

liveCommentary.text:
The track temperature peaked at 46 Degrees Celsius earlier, it is now down to 42 Degrees. So yes it is still roasting hot, but the teams notice every small change and collect the data accordingly.  
  
  
The best conditions will be later on once the sun sets, with around 90 minutes to go in the session.
liveCommentary.title: Temperatures slowly cooling off

liveCommentary.text:
Hello and welcome back to live coverage of the final session from pre-season testing in Bahrain.   
  
  
The sun is still shining, it is still roasting hot and the teams have just four hours left to test out everything they need to before these cars hit the track in Melbourne in a couple of weeks,,,
liveCommentary.title: Welcome back to Bahrain

liveCommentary.text:
We are taking a short break, but we will be back with live coverage of the afternoon session from Bahrain.  
  
  
A few teams need to complete their seat swaps, Mercedes need to finish that PU change and then we will have plenty of cars back out on track for the final time in this second pre-season test.
liveCommentary.title: Join us again soon

liveCommentary.text:
Leclerc topped the morning session for Ferrari, thanks to that earlier 1m 33.689s, finishing ahead of Antonelli and Piastri.  
  
  
The Ferrari man did not top the lap count in the end though, as he was just pipped by Ocon who managed a very impressive 82 laps, to Leclerc's 80.
liveCommentary.title: Leclerc on top in the morning session

liveCommentary.text:
Well - Piastri got a good launch there, and took the fight to Ocon. Which is interesting, as Haas yesterday had a great launch in both practice starts.  
  
  
So, Ferrari have nailed the starts, Haas have been looking good and now McLaren seem to have cracked the code too.
liveCommentary.title: McLaren look good off the line

liveCommentary.text: The clock has hit zero, with Ocon, Piastri and Hadjar coming out for the practice start. It looks like Ocon is going to line up on pole here - although we may first get an extra Formation Lap like yesterday.
liveCommentary.title: Three cars head back out

liveCommentary.text: As mentioned, the systems checks are now being completed so we do have red flag conditions. As such, the cars all slowly head back to the pit lane - but they will be back out soon for those practice starts.
liveCommentary.title: Out come the red flags

liveCommentary.text:
Stroll is back out for Aston Martin, on the medium tyre. But this run might be short-lived, as often Race Control run tests of their own in the final moments of a session, cycling through yellow flag, red flag and VSC periods.   
  
  
Stroll has just run wide through Turns 11 and 13, and then he returns to the pits.
liveCommentary.title: Into the last ten minutes

liveCommentary.text:
The Canadian is out for Aston Martin, but it is only an installation lap and he soon returns to the pit lane.  
  
  
Hopefully they can get a bit more running in in the second session, and collect more of that crucial data de la Rosa mentioned earlier.  
  
  
There are two weeks to go until the first race, so there is time for some fixes for anyone who is struggling with gremlins at the moment.
liveCommentary.title: Stroll emerges for Aston Martin

liveCommentary.text:
"It was a loss of pneumatic pressure for Kimi Antonelli earlier, which forced him to stop out on track earlier. The team are switching the PU, which means running is over for Antonelli. George Russell will be in this afternoon, once the car is ready to go," reports Lawrence Barretto.  
  
  
That is bad news for the youngster then, who as well as lost running, misses out on the opportunity to practice a start too.
liveCommentary.title: An update on Mercedes

liveCommentary.text:
How Hadjar gets on against Verstappen this season will be fascinating - and in some ways, he has an easier task than some of his predecessors.   
  
  
That is because he is up against Verstappen in new cars for them both. But, and there is always a but. The Dutchman has been supremely fast in every generation of F1 car he has driven, and also across other series.   
  
  
What would be a good result for Hadjar? Well, qualifying in Q3 for starters, and scoring points in Melbourne has to be seen as a solid start.  
  
  
Longer term, Red Bull want a driver who consistently contributes points in the Teams' Championship.
liveCommentary.title: Hadjar returns to the fray

liveCommentary.text: Stroll is suited and booted, and he is sitting in the cockpit of his Aston Martin. While he has not been out yet, it certainly looks like the team are trying to get the Canadian out soon. Which is good news, even if it is just for a few installation laps to check the work they have completed on the car.
liveCommentary.title: Good news for Aston Martin

liveCommentary.text:
There are seven cars out on track, and one we haven't mentioned much today is Sainz at Williams. He is in the car all day today, and has completed 55 laps so far.  
  
  
Williams were playing catch up after missing the Barcelona Shakedown, and while they have definitely caught up in terms of mileage, there are some question marks over how fast the car is.  
  
  
The same can be said for much of the midfield though - one expert will say a team is definitely at the top of the midfield pecking order, the next picks a completely different team.  
  
  
The things we know are the Mercedes engine looks fairly reliable - unless Antonelli's earlier issue turns out to be PU related - so on that front, Williams are in a good position, but this year their midfield rivals Alpine are also running a Mercedes PU, so they lose that advantage over the French team.
liveCommentary.title: Seven cars out on track

liveCommentary.text:
Just a reminder that six teams are swapping their drivers at lunchtime, so for the likes of Piastri and Hadjar, this is their last running before Melbourne.   
  
  
That is why we have not seen an many aero rakes this morning - the teams are really trying to dial in on those race set-ups now, with all attention swiftly turning to Australia and the opening weekend of the season.
liveCommentary.title: The last running for some

liveCommentary.text:
Three hours gone, one to go. Leclerc remains top of the timing sheets with a 1m 33.689s, two tenths faster than Antonelli who remains in the pits for the time being.  
  
  
Piastri is third, the Australian having hit a half-century of laps - but it is Leclerc leading the way with 66 and counting.   
  
  
And as for the conditions, it is scorching out there. The track is up at 46 Degrees Celsius right now, so the drivers will really be feeling these longer stints.
liveCommentary.title: One hour left of the morning session

liveCommentary.text:
"A little more on Ferrari's experimental 'upside down' rear wing, which got the paddock talking yesterday. The team have reiterated that it is very much a test item, with several steps to go through before confirming the design as race-ready," says Mike Seymour.  
  
  
"Time will tell where and when it might re-appear as the season gets under way, with the FIA yesterday communicating their view that it is legal. Lewis Hamilton's 'Active Aero' running gave the team some valuable early data, with engineers at the track taking plenty of notes and the numbers now being evaluated back at Maranello.   
  
  
"Ferrari also confirmed that a sensor issue interrupted their programme yesterday, but today has been smoother so far – race runs currently the focus in these hot temperatures."
liveCommentary.title: Ferrari and their innovative rear wing

liveCommentary.text:
Shrouded in black drapes, the Mercedes is wheeled back into the garage so they can start work on diagnosing and fixing the issue.  
  
  
And speaking of issues, McLaren have fixed theirs - so Piastri is back out, looking to add to his tally of 38 laps.
liveCommentary.title: The W17 makes it back

liveCommentary.text:
"Yesterday we had some battery issues on Fernando's car, and Honda are carrying out some tests. Due to that, and to the fact we have a shortage of parts, we will do some limited running today. They will be short, and they will be separated by at least half an hour to look into some things," explains Pedro de la Rosa, Team Ambassador for Aston Martin.   
  
  
"We are not where we wanted to be, we hoped to have done a lot more [laps]. But even so, we have an enormous amount of data to look into ahead of Australia.  
  
  
"We do know the areas of the car to focus on. It is not where we wanted to be, but the laps we have done are showing us a direction to go in."
liveCommentary.title: A further update from Aston Martin

liveCommentary.text:
So, Aston Martin are still working on their car, Mercedes are waiting to get hold of theirs, and now McLaren are working on the MCL40. There are some mechanics around the rear of the papaya car while Piastri watches on.   
  
  
We'll let you know how much time they lose here...
liveCommentary.title: Piastri remains in the pits

liveCommentary.text:
And right on cue, the lights go green. Gasly leads the way out for Alpine, Ocon and Lindblad also heading straight back out.   
  
  
Perez is also heading out to add to his eight laps, as he pulls over to complete a practice start.
liveCommentary.title: Back to green light conditions

liveCommentary.text: The Italian is getting a lift back to the pits, and his car has been pushed behind the barriers for now. So, it remains to be seen how long it will take to get that onto a flat-bed truck and get it back to the pits, but it does mean the session can resume quite swiftly.
liveCommentary.title: Antonelli gets a lift

liveCommentary.text:
Antonelli has stopped out on track, and he is out of the car as the red flags fly. Mercedes can join the lost time club today then, although it remains to be seen just how much time they will lose here.   
  
  
Antonelli has completed 49 laps so far.
liveCommentary.title: The red flags are out for Mercedes

liveCommentary.text:
Over halfway through the session, and Aston Martin continue to lose time here. This is far from ideal, not the mention the fact that when they do come out, they will only do short stints - so no race simulation runs ahead of Melbourne.   
  
  
What is going through Alonso's mind? He turns 45 in July this year, and has made no secret that he is not here to make up the numbers.  
  
  
How long before this car catches up to the rest? Adrian Newey will be hard at work behind the scenes, so there is no shortage of brain power being applied to thinking of fixes...
liveCommentary.title: Still no Aston Martin

liveCommentary.text:
"Checked in at Mercedes and they're feeling pretty satisfied with their week's work. It was a tricky first pre-season test for the team in Bahrain, with some gremlins interrupting their run plans – particularly during Kimi Antonelli's allocated sessions," explains F1.com's Mike Seymour.  
  
  
"But they've made up for lost mileage over the last couple of days and should get through their full programme if all goes to plan this afternoon.   
  
  
"The focus now is on working through a range of set-ups and learning more about the W17 in different configurations. All the signs are pointing towards them being in a top four group with Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren. In what order? We'll have to wait for Australia..."
liveCommentary.title: An update from the paddock

liveCommentary.text:
Perez is finally back out for Cadillac, on the C2 harder tyres. He has lost plenty of running this morning, but has time to make up some of those laps.   
  
  
The Mexican was only out of the sport for one season, so shouldn't be too rusty heading into Australia - his team mate Bottas was also on the sidelines for just the one year.
liveCommentary.title: Cadillac head back out

liveCommentary.text:
Lindblad is joining Antonelli on the grid this season - those two with a combined age of 37 years old, younger than Alonso (44), Hamilton (41) and Hulkenberg (38).   
  
  
So, now you all feel old, let's look at Lindblad. He is the only rookie this season, but while he needs to learn some of the tracks, at least the cars this year are new for everyone.   
  
  
He has looked good so far, but the real test will be going up against team mate Lawson in a race and seeing how he stacks up.
liveCommentary.title: Two teenagers on the grid

liveCommentary.text:
Mercedes managed an awful lot of laps at the Barcelona Shakedown, but last week did not quite go to plan - one PU change in session meant a lot of laps missed.  
  
  
But this week has been relative plain sailing. They managed 304 laps across the last two days, and already Antonelli is on 39 this morning.   
  
  
A race distance here is 57 laps, and it looks like the teenager might be on a race simulation run here, as he is lapping consistently in the 1m 37's.
liveCommentary.title: Antonelli's lap count

liveCommentary.text:
Piastri locks up on his latest run on the medium tyres. We have seen a lot of lock ups this week, as drivers experiment with braking points and also search for grip with the new tyres.  
  
  
Pirelli have developed tyres for this season that are narrower than last year's, to the tune of 25mm at the front and 30mm at the back. They are also a bit lighter too, to buy into the 'nimble' car concept for 2026.   
  
  
So, as well as all the other learning, the drivers need to adjust to life on the new Pirelli tyres too.
liveCommentary.title: Piastri locks up

liveCommentary.text:
Pirelli gave the teams a choice from all five compounds this week - last week, the teams only had the C1, C2 and C3 tyres to play with.  
  
  
They do still have a total allocation, but had free choice within that in how many sets to bring of each tyre. And as you can see, there was some variance within the teams over who fancied running what.   
  
  
Mercedes did not bring any of the C4 or C5 compounds, so Antonelli is out on the C3 at the moment and that is effectively their 'soft' tyre for the week.
liveCommentary.title: A word on the tyres

liveCommentary.text: Cadillac have Perez in the car this morning, but he has managed just the one installation lap. Like Aston Martin, Cadillac have had some reliability woes this week and have only managed 167 laps going into today - the second lowest of anyone, Aston Martin the only team with less laps.
liveCommentary.title: Cadillac also struggling

liveCommentary.text:
Yes, the track temperature has gone over 40 Degrees Celsius. Yes, it is hot, dry and sunny.  
  
  
And yet, Ocon is out on the intermediate tyre. This is purely data gathering - in wet conditions, the teams will be allowed to still flatten the front wing, but not the back, similar to the way DRS was disabled in the wet.  
  
  
Ocon is squirrely his way around the track, those tyres will not last long but he is gathering valuable data for both the team and for the FIA in terms of Active Aero working how it should.
liveCommentary.title: Ocon comes out on intermediate tyres

liveCommentary.text:
Jolyon Palmer is trackside, and he has updated on the conditions - hotter, but no wind. That is interesting, as the open parts of this track are often susceptible to some breezy conditions.  
  
  
So far across both tests, what seems clear is that while wind is still a factor, these cars are not as heavily affected as their predecessors.   
  
  
The heat though, that will be leading to heavily tyre degradation - especially in any car running a very heavy fuel load.
liveCommentary.title: No wind and a bit hotter

liveCommentary.text:
Uh oh - the screens are up at Aston Martin. That means the floor is off the car, and that means whatever is going on is quite a sizeable issue.  
  
  
Alonso was in the car yesterday, and he stopped out on track in the afternoon session. The team did not reveal the exact cause of that stoppage but Honda - who supply the power units to Aston Martin - did reveal the issue.  
  
  
But the sum total is that Stroll is losing valuable track time here.
liveCommentary.title: The screens are up at Aston Martin

liveCommentary.text:
While the teams keep some of the details of their programmes under wraps, and will also 'sand bag' to hide performance, one thing most people can agree on is that Aston Martin are struggling.  
  
  
They recorded the fewest laps of any team yesterday, and are also trailing when you add up the total mileage this week.  
  
  
And they are the only team yet to make it out on track today, with the tell-tale wall of mechanics blocking the car at the moment as they do some work on it.
liveCommentary.title: No sign of Aston Martin

liveCommentary.text:
So, looking at the early times - Leclerc is on top with a 1m 33.689s. A little time to find to get tot he times we saw yesterday, but that is to be expected as it is still hot out there.  
  
  
Representative conditions will be a little later on once the sun sets, with the race here beginning in twilight, just before sunset.  
  
  
Piastri is second at the moment, Ocon third and Hadjar fourth.
liveCommentary.title: Leclerc on top at the moment

liveCommentary.text:
The drivers got two cracks at a race start yesterday, at the end of each session. And Hamilton really did impress in both. Ferrari seem to have developed a car that gets away really quickly, with minimal wheel spin.   
  
  
We will have to wait a few hours to see if Leclerc can do likewise, with Race Control allowing for a standing start in the final few moments of the session.
liveCommentary.title: Hamilton impresses off the line

liveCommentary.text:
If Ferrari use that wing in the first few races, then we'll have an answer as to the cost benefit analysis, as they have tested out a more conventional Active Aero opening system here too.   
  
  
But then, will anyone else copy that system?  
  
  
James Vowles admitted yesterday that his team had not thought up that method, and said both his team and likely every other team would be crunching the data last night to see if it is worth pursuing this season.  
  
  
So, we will have to see how this plays out. But that rear wing is not the only impressive thing about the Ferrari in testing.
liveCommentary.title: Ferrari cause a stir

liveCommentary.text:
We said we would talk more about Ferrari's rear wing today, so here goes. Yesterday morning, Hamilton came out, debuted a new rear wing mechanism and then parked up with a reliability issue for the rest of the morning.  
  
  
While there is some variance in the way the teams have opted to use Active Aero, with some rear wings opening from the top, some from the halfway point, and some from the bottom, what Ferrari did was entirely different.  
  
  
They have found a loophole that allows the mechanism to flip over. But does it reduce drag even more, or does the extra split second to get it back into place lose them more than it gains?
liveCommentary.title: Ferrari steal a march on the rest - or do they?!

liveCommentary.text:
It is 25 Degrees Celsius here, and the track is at 33 Degrees - expect that to rise as this morning wears on.  
  
  
The temperatures are not bothering the teams, the mechanics are working hard and plenty of drivers are straight out and running.  
  
  
Gasly is sporting some aero rakes on his Alpine, while Lindblad has just locked up and run wide. All go here, as Hadjar joins the fray.
liveCommentary.title: Another glorious day in Bahrain

liveCommentary.text: The morning session is underway - the lights go green at the end of the pit lane, and there is immediate action. Lindblad is out, so are Ocon, Leclerc and Antonelli.
liveCommentary.title: That's the green light

liveCommentary.text:
Yesterday, Ferrari unveiled a new rear wing Active Aero mechanism, which seemed to fully rotate the component down the straights. It caused plenty of chatter in the paddock and pit lane - at testing, someone always brings something that gets everyone talking.  
  
  
We will explain more about it as the session gets underway, but never fear - we will watch out for it closely and let you know if it is in use again today.
liveCommentary.title: Ferrari and the rotating rear wing

liveCommentary.text:
The teams can only run one car in testing, so some split their allocation of sessions by day and some change over at lunchtime.  
  
  
Either way, today's full driver line up can be found here.  
  
  
Five teams are running just the one driver, six are splitting shifts today - so Charles Leclerc, Lance Stroll, Carlos Sainz, Arvid Lindblad and Pierre Gasly get full driving duties today.
liveCommentary.title: Who is driving today?

liveCommentary.text:
This is the sixth and final day of testing - after today, the next time the cars will be on track will be in Melbourne.   
  
  
As such, the teams will be throwing everything they have at today to make sure they have learned as much as possible - so absolutely no one will want a reliability gremlin to pop up.
liveCommentary.title: One last day awaits

liveCommentary.text: Hello and welcome back to Bahrain, ahead of the final day of pre-season testing...
liveCommentary.title: Welcome back to Bahrain

liveCommentary.text:
**•****Day 3 of the second pre-season test comes from Bahrain**  
**• Charles Leclerc wound upfastest overall for Ferrari**  
**• Aston Martin had a tricky session and only managed a handful of laps before ending their day early**  
**• The next time the cars will be in action is in Australia on March 06**
liveCommentary.title: Overview
